reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 3, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: It never bends or changes direction. Is it a straight line or a curved line?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Straight line (seeds 42, 43, 46), flat surface (seed 45), and curved surface (seed 44) are all correctly identified as the correct_answer at least once, but 'curved line' is never the correct_answer anywhere in the 5 samples -- it appears only as a wrong-option distractor.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Of the four concepts the competency names (straight lines, curved lines, flat surfaces, curved surfaces), curved lines are the one concept never generated as the tested/correct case, leaving that quarter of the competency's scope unassessed.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Descriptive clues like 'like a ball' (seed 44) and 'like a tabletop' (seed 45) give Grade 2 students concrete real-world anchors for abstract geometric vocabulary.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The identical stem 'It never bends or changes direction. Is it a straight line or a curved line?' repeats verbatim at seeds 42, 43, and 46, so 3 of 5 samples are not distinct variants.

competency_alignment.rationale: All five samples build straight/curved/flat classification directly, without drifting into an unrelated shape-naming or measurement axis.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency does not specify a numeric range, and the qualitative descriptions used (bends all the way around, no bumps or curves) stay within Grade 2 Quarter 4's conceptual scope.
